## Claims
- [source-backed] The authors reported computational verification for bigrassmannian cases with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-6, lines 48-52]
- [proved] The requested regressions hold by vertical Pieri:
  \[
  s_{(1,1)}s_{(1)}=s_{(2,1)}+s_{(1,1,1)},\qquad
  s_{(1,1)}s_{(2)}=s_{(3,1)}+s_{(2,1,1)}.
  \]
  Hence \(c_{(1,1),(1)}^{(3)}=0\) and \(c_{(1,1),(2)}^{(2,2)}=0\).
- [computed] Using the accepted LR presentation of \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), a right-to-left row-reading LR-tableau enumerator and integral SNF calculation returned torsion-free quotients \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^d\) for all 90 rectangular instances in \(\{r\le5,q=n-r\le6\}\setminus\{r\le4,q\le5\}\). In each row below, entries are \(d\), with columns \(i=1,\ldots,q-1\) and rows \(j=1,\ldots,r-1\):
  \[
  \begin{array}{c|c|c}
  (r,q)&j& (d_i)_i\\ \hline
  (2,6)&1&(2,2,2,2,2)\\ \hline
  (3,6)&1&(3,3,3,3,2)\\
       &2&(2,3,3,3,3)\\ \hline
  (4,6)&1&(4,4,4,3,2)\\
       &2&(3,6,6,6,3)\\
       &3&(2,3,4,4,4)\\ \hline
  (5,2)&1,2,3,4&(2)\\ \hline
  (5,3)&1&(3,2)\\
       &2&(3,3)\\
       &3&(3,3)\\
       &4&(2,3)\\ \hline
  (5,4)&1&(4,3,2)\\
       &2&(4,6,3)\\
       &3&(3,6,4)\\
       &4&(2,3,4)\\ \hline
  (5,5)&1&(5,4,3,2)\\
       &2&(4,10,6,3)\\
       &3&(3,6,10,4)\\
       &4&(2,3,4,5)\\ \hline
  (5,6)&1&(5,5,4,3,2)\\
       &2&(4,10,10,6,3)\\
       &3&(3,6,10,10,4)\\
       &4&(2,3,4,5,5)
  \end{array}
  \]
  Every displayed \(d\) equals
  \[
  \binom{\min(q-i,r-j)+\min(i,j)}{\min(q-i,r-j)}.
  \]
  [artifact ce9dca58d3924029b4839d830f43cfe6514239f9a1025dc2f51a2e1c9bb3fedb]
- [proved] For any tabulated instance, the accepted \(N=d\)-element Schur generating families are irredundant: their images span \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), whereas \(N-1\) elements cannot span \(\mathbb Z^N\); graded Nakayama then implies that no generator can be deleted.
- [unsupported] The retained sandbox artifact does not document a second independently implemented LR/SNF computation, nor Pieri-based verification of all 90 SNF outputs. Thus the requested independent reproduction of every finite result remains unverified.

## Strategy
Construct the relation matrix with columns indexed by \(\mu\) satisfying \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\), and rows
\[
r_{\lambda,\mu}=\sum_{\nu}c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}e_\nu
\]
for nonempty \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\), retaining only \(\nu\subseteq q^r\). Enumerate LR tableaux in top-to-bottom rows, filling each row right-to-left, enforcing semistandard and lattice-word conditions. Compute the integral SNF of this matrix.

## Gaps
- The finite computation does not prove the conjecture beyond the 90 enumerated rectangular instances.
- The supplied context does not identify these rectangular \((r,q,i,j)\) data bijectively with admissible \(v_{r,s,t,n}\).
- Independent replication of the SNF outputs is missing.

## Next
Run a separately implemented LR/Pieri multiplication routine and independently compute the 90 relation matrices and SNFs; compare invariant factors entrywise with the table above.
